name: SupermarketShoppingThisOrThatProduct

custom.system_prompt:
You are generating realistic near-future supermarket shopping conversations. Using Sigma is completely normal. Sigma can see the products the users are holding — labels, ingredients, descriptions. VA interactions are brief and specific.

Write dialogue that sounds like real people. Hard rules:
- Every line must be under 70 characters. Split longer thoughts.
- The debate about two products is genuine — they have real reasons for their preferences
- Sigma answers product comparison questions in two sentences maximum
- After Sigma answers, they still have to decide — information doesn't always settle it

sound_effects_config.prompt: Supermarket ambience, background store music, bottles clinking on shelf, quiet background chatter

initial_prompt:
Generate a conversation where Fiona and Ruben are standing in front of two similar products — olive oil, pasta, a dairy alternative, or similar — and can't agree. Ruben has a chef's perspective, Fiona reads labels carefully (she checks for hidden gluten). They debate, then ask Sigma to help them compare. Sigma can see both products. They get an answer but still have to argue about it a bit before deciding. A second, briefer product question comes up later.

Hard rules:
- Every line under 70 characters
- The debate is genuine — both have valid points
- Sigma answers specifically: compares the products on the relevant dimension
- The decision takes longer than it should — that's the joke

user1.name: Fiona
user1.tts_prompt: Direct and warm, natural Dublin accent

user2.name: Ruben
user2.tts_prompt: Warm and unhurried, mild Portuguese accent

variations.context: Standing in an aisle comparing two similar products — neither can fully commit

setting.mood: Amused stand-off. Both right about different things.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Couple with strong independent opinions about food — frequently, both are right
setting.background: Ruben brings professional instinct. Fiona brings label literacy and celiac vigilance. They do this every week.
setting.conversation_style: Pointed but affectionate. Quick back-and-forth. Sigma is the tiebreaker they don't fully trust.

scenario_template.topic: Both pick up a different version of the same product and immediately disagree
scenario_template.note: Fiona is reading the label. Ruben has a professional opinion about the brand or origin. Neither is backing down yet.

scenario_template.topic: Each makes their case — Ruben on quality/taste, Fiona on ingredients/price/safety
scenario_template.note: Brief, punchy lines. They know each other's arguments. No real anger.

scenario_template.topic: Fiona asks Sigma to compare — Sigma can see both products
scenario_template.note: Sigma gives a clear, specific comparison — production method, ingredient difference, or relevant fact. Two sentences max.

scenario_template.topic: Sigma's answer didn't fully settle it — they each interpret it differently
scenario_template.note: Ruben uses the answer to support his position. Fiona finds a counterpoint. The decision is made eventually, without ceremony.
Ruben shares a funny memory related to snacking as a kid, causing both to momentarily forget the standoff.
Fiona points out an unfamiliar product on the shelf, suggesting they try it as an alternative.
Ruben raises a concern about gluten content, and Fiona reassures him by checking the label details.

scenario_template.topic: Disagreement about another product from the shelves
scenario_template.note: They lightly argue about the presence of sugar in a different snack, highlighting differing tolerances.
They pivot from the disagreement to plan an upcoming meal, eventually agreeing on a shared favorite.

scenario_template.topic: Later in the shop — a second, quicker product question to Sigma
scenario_template.note: Sigma answers. They accept it and move on. No extended debate.

user1.name: Fiona
user1.role: Reads labels carefully — both for celiac reasons and general curiosity. Direct. Will use Sigma to get facts rather than opinions. Wins arguments on technicalities.

user2.name: Ruben
user2.role: Former chef — has strong instincts about quality and origin. Trusts his palate over labels. Warm about it, not arrogant. Loses food arguments to Fiona about 40% of the time.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Product comparison assistant. Can read both labels. Gives factual, specific comparisons — production method, ingredient list differences, relevant quality markers. Does not take sides.

conversation_structure: The product debate is the center — it runs for several turns before Sigma is called.
After Sigma answers, the debate continues briefly — information is not automatically decisive.
Both characters have valid perspectives. Neither is clearly wrong.
Fiona's celiac awareness should appear naturally — she checks for gluten without making it the entire topic.
The second product question is shorter and more decisive than the first.
assistant_behavior: Sigma compares the specific products in front of them — no generic advice.
Sigma answers in two sentences maximum.
Sigma does not recommend one over the other — gives facts and lets them decide.
Sigma can reference what it sees on the labels.
